question: A prairie plant doses alum into raw water with alkalinity of 40 mg/L as CaCO3. Which input should the operator check before raising the alum dose further?
correctAnswer: The remaining alkalinity available to buffer the reaction
explanation: Alum hydrolysis consumes alkalinity, so a low alkalinity water has little buffering left and its pH can fall if the dose rises.
options: The remaining alkalinity available to buffer the reaction
The colour of the finished water storage tank paint
The speed rating printed on the raw water pump motor
The age of the alum delivery truck used that week
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Coagulation Chemistry and Alkalinity. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: The remaining alkalinity available to buffer the reaction
optionB: The colour of the finished water storage tank paint
optionC: The speed rating printed on the raw water pump motor
optionD: The age of the alum delivery truck used that week

question: In a standard jar test series, which variable is changed from jar to jar while mixing and settling conditions stay the same?
correctAnswer: The coagulant dose added to each jar
explanation: A jar test holds raw water, mixing and settling constant and varies the chemical dose so the doses can be compared fairly.
options: The size of the beakers used in the test
The coagulant dose added to each jar
The temperature of the laboratory room
The brand of stirrer paddle in each jar
sourceTitle: WPI: operator examination references — laboratory and treatment study resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Jar Test Dose Selection. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: The size of the beakers used in the test
optionB: The coagulant dose added to each jar
optionC: The temperature of the laboratory room
optionD: The brand of stirrer paddle in each jar

question: A settling basin is fitted with inclined tubes. Which component change gives the basin more effective settling area in the same footprint?
correctAnswer: Adding more inclined tube modules across the basin width
explanation: Inclined tubes add shallow settling surfaces, so particles settle a short distance onto a tube surface instead of the basin floor.
options: Raising the raw water inlet gate by one full turn
Painting the basin walls a darker colour for contrast
Adding more inclined tube modules across the basin width
Lengthening the sludge scraper chain on the floor
sourceTitle: US EPA: Surface Water Treatment Rules — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Tube and Plate Settlers. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Raising the raw water inlet gate by one full turn
optionB: Painting the basin walls a darker colour for contrast
optionC: Adding more inclined tube modules across the basin width
optionD: Lengthening the sludge scraper chain on the floor

question: A dual media filter bed is built from two materials. Which pairing and order, from top to bottom, is correct?
correctAnswer: Coarser, lighter anthracite over finer, denser sand
explanation: Anthracite is coarser and lighter, so it stays on top after backwashing, while the finer, denser sand settles below it.
options: Coarser, lighter anthracite under finer, denser sand
Fine silica sand over coarse rounded river gravel
Crushed limestone over a deep layer of anthracite
Coarser, lighter anthracite over finer, denser sand
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Dual Media Filtration. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Coarser, lighter anthracite under finer, denser sand
optionB: Fine silica sand over coarse rounded river gravel
optionC: Crushed limestone over a deep layer of anthracite
optionD: Coarser, lighter anthracite over finer, denser sand

question: An operator calculates CT for a clearwell segment. Which two measured inputs does the CT value combine?
correctAnswer: Free chlorine residual and the T10 contact time
explanation: CT is the product of the disinfectant residual concentration and the T10 contact time for the segment.
options: Free chlorine residual and the T10 contact time
Raw water turbidity and the filter run length
Chlorine dose applied and the tank paint colour
Water temperature alone and the basin depth
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: CT With Baffling Factors. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Free chlorine residual and the T10 contact time
optionB: Raw water turbidity and the filter run length
optionC: Chlorine dose applied and the tank paint colour
optionD: Water temperature alone and the basin depth

question: Raw water entering a plant contains ammonia. As chlorine is first added, which sequence describes what happens to the measured free chlorine residual?
correctAnswer: It stays near zero while combined chlorine forms first
explanation: Chlorine reacts with ammonia to form chloramines, so free residual stays near zero until the demand is worked through toward breakpoint.
options: It rises immediately in step with the dose applied
It stays near zero while combined chlorine forms first
It turns into fluoride before any reaction occurs
It is removed by the filter media within minutes
sourceTitle: US EPA: Surface Water Treatment Rules — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Breakpoint Chlorination. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: It rises immediately in step with the dose applied
optionB: It stays near zero while combined chlorine forms first
optionC: It turns into fluoride before any reaction occurs
optionD: It is removed by the filter media within minutes

question: During an alkalinity titration, which observation tells the operator the endpoint of the titration has been reached?
correctAnswer: The indicator colour change at the target pH value
explanation: The endpoint is signalled by the indicator colour change that corresponds to the target pH for the titration being performed.
options: The burette becoming too heavy to hold steadily
The sample starting to boil in the flask bottom
The indicator colour change at the target pH value
The stir bar stopping at the side of the flask
sourceTitle: WPI: operator examination references — laboratory and treatment study resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Laboratory Titrations. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: The burette becoming too heavy to hold steadily
optionB: The sample starting to boil in the flask bottom
optionC: The indicator colour change at the target pH value
optionD: The stir bar stopping at the side of the flask

question: A delivery of chlorine gas cylinders arrives at a small plant. Which storage step comes before the cylinders are put into service?
correctAnswer: Securing each cylinder upright so it cannot fall over
explanation: Compressed gas cylinders are chained or otherwise secured upright so they cannot tip, fall and damage a valve.
options: Removing the valve protection caps for the whole shift
Stacking the cylinders flat in two layers for storage
Storing the cylinders beside the ammonia solution tank
Securing each cylinder upright so it cannot fall over
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Confined Spaces
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Chemical Storage and Handling. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Removing the valve protection caps for the whole shift
optionB: Stacking the cylinders flat in two layers for storage
optionC: Storing the cylinders beside the ammonia solution tank
optionD: Securing each cylinder upright so it cannot fall over

question: After an alum dose increase, a plant sees pH fall from 7.4 to 6.6 and floc becomes small and weak. What is the most likely cause the operator should address first?
correctAnswer: Alkalinity was consumed faster than the water could buffer it
explanation: Alum consumes alkalinity as it hydrolyses; when alkalinity runs short, pH drops and charge neutralisation and floc formation suffer.
options: Alkalinity was consumed faster than the water could buffer it
The rapid mix motor was turning in the wrong direction
The settled water launders were cleaned too recently
The raw water pump was drawing from a deeper intake
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Coagulation Chemistry and Alkalinity. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Alkalinity was consumed faster than the water could buffer it
optionB: The rapid mix motor was turning in the wrong direction
optionC: The settled water launders were cleaned too recently
optionD: The raw water pump was drawing from a deeper intake

question: Jar test results show settled turbidity of 8, 4, 2 and 5 NTU at doses of 20, 30, 40 and 50 mg/L. Which dose should the operator carry into the plant trial?
correctAnswer: The 40 mg/L dose, which gave the lowest settled turbidity
explanation: The dose giving the lowest settled turbidity, 40 mg/L here, is the starting point for the plant trial, then it is confirmed at full scale.
options: The 50 mg/L dose, because the highest dose is safest
The 40 mg/L dose, which gave the lowest settled turbidity
The 20 mg/L dose, because it uses the least chemical
The 30 mg/L dose, because it sits mid range overall
sourceTitle: WPI: operator examination references — laboratory and treatment study resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Jar Test Dose Selection. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: The 50 mg/L dose, because the highest dose is safest
optionB: The 40 mg/L dose, which gave the lowest settled turbidity
optionC: The 20 mg/L dose, because it uses the least chemical
optionD: The 30 mg/L dose, because it sits mid range overall

question: A plate settler basin shows sludge sliding poorly and building up on the plates during cold weather. Which adjustment addresses the buildup most directly?
correctAnswer: Cleaning the plate surfaces and checking the plate spacing
explanation: Sludge that does not slide off inclined plates is usually a fouling or spacing problem, so cleaning and checking the plates comes first.
options: Raising the plant flow rate to push the sludge through
Adding more coagulant so the sludge layer grows heavier
Cleaning the plate surfaces and checking the plate spacing
Lowering the basin water level below the plate tops
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Tube and Plate Settlers. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Raising the plant flow rate to push the sludge through
optionB: Adding more coagulant so the sludge layer grows heavier
optionC: Cleaning the plate surfaces and checking the plate spacing
optionD: Lowering the basin water level below the plate tops

question: A dual media filter passes fine particles early in the run but its head loss climbs slowly. Which bed condition best explains this pattern?
correctAnswer: The anthracite layer is too shallow to trap fine material
explanation: The coarse anthracite top layer does the depth trapping; if it is too shallow, fine particles pass through before straining builds up.
options: The sand layer has completely turned into mud balls
The underdrain laterals are plugged with coarse gravel
The backwash troughs are set below the media surface
The anthracite layer is too shallow to trap fine material
sourceTitle: US EPA: Surface Water Treatment Rules — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Dual Media Filtration. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: The sand layer has completely turned into mud balls
optionB: The underdrain laterals are plugged with coarse gravel
optionC: The backwash troughs are set below the media surface
optionD: The anthracite layer is too shallow to trap fine material

question: A clearwell is operated at a lower water level than the tracer study condition. What happens to the credited CT for the same chlorine residual?
correctAnswer: It falls, because the shorter contact time lowers T10
explanation: A lower level reduces the volume and the T10 time, so the same residual produces a smaller CT product.
options: It falls, because the shorter contact time lowers T10
It rises, because less water dilutes the chlorine dose
It stays equal, because residual alone sets the CT
It doubles, because baffling improves at low levels
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: CT With Baffling Factors. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: It falls, because the shorter contact time lowers T10
optionB: It rises, because less water dilutes the chlorine dose
optionC: It stays equal, because residual alone sets the CT
optionD: It doubles, because baffling improves at low levels

question: An operator raising the chlorine dose sees combined residual climb, then fall, while free residual stays near zero. What does the falling combined residual indicate?
correctAnswer: Chloramines are being oxidised as breakpoint is approached
explanation: Past the hump of the breakpoint curve, added chlorine oxidises the chloramines, so combined residual falls before free residual appears.
options: The chlorine feed pump has lost its prime completely
Chloramines are being oxidised as breakpoint is approached
Ammonia is being added somewhere in the clearwell
The sample was taken from the wrong sampling tap
sourceTitle: US EPA: Surface Water Treatment Rules — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Breakpoint Chlorination. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: The chlorine feed pump has lost its prime completely
optionB: Chloramines are being oxidised as breakpoint is approached
optionC: Ammonia is being added somewhere in the clearwell
optionD: The sample was taken from the wrong sampling tap

question: A hardness titration keeps overshooting the endpoint and the results vary between repeats. Which technique change improves the titration most directly?
correctAnswer: Adding titrant drop by drop near the endpoint while swirling
explanation: Approaching the endpoint slowly, drop by drop with constant swirling, prevents overshoot and makes repeat results agree.
options: Shaking the flask hard after every single drop added
Using a much larger sample so the colour looks darker
Adding titrant drop by drop near the endpoint while swirling
Reading the burette from above instead of eye level
sourceTitle: WPI: operator examination references — laboratory and treatment study resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Laboratory Titrations. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Shaking the flask hard after every single drop added
optionB: Using a much larger sample so the colour looks darker
optionC: Adding titrant drop by drop near the endpoint while swirling
optionD: Reading the burette from above instead of eye level

question: A bulk hypochlorite tank is being filled from a delivery truck. Which step protects the plant if the tank is overfilled during the transfer?
correctAnswer: Watching the level and having the overflow routed to containment
explanation: Monitoring the level during transfer and routing any overflow into secondary containment keeps a spill from reaching soil or drains.
options: Closing the containment drain so nothing can leave the area
Filling the tank at night so fewer staff are nearby
Removing the level gauge so the driver works by sound
Watching the level and having the overflow routed to containment

optionA: Closing the containment drain so nothing can leave the area

optionD: Watching the level and having the overflow routed to containment

question: Spring runoff raises raw water colour and turbidity sharply while alkalinity stays moderate. Which coagulation response fits this change best?
correctAnswer: Raising the coagulant dose and confirming it with jar tests
explanation: Higher colour and turbidity raise coagulant demand, so the dose is increased and the new dose is verified with jar tests on the changed water.
options: Raising the coagulant dose and confirming it with jar tests
Cutting the coagulant dose to save chemical during runoff
Switching the plant to direct filtration for the season
Holding the winter dose and waiting for the runoff to pass

optionB: Cutting the coagulant dose to save chemical during runoff

question: Two jar test runs on the same raw water give different best doses a day apart. Which check should the operator make before trusting either result?
correctAnswer: Whether the raw water sample and stock solution were fresh
explanation: Stale samples and degraded stock solutions change results, so freshness of the sample and the chemical stock is checked first.
options: Whether the laboratory lights were on during the first run
Whether the raw water sample and stock solution were fresh
Whether the beakers were dried in the same rack order
Whether the same operator poured every jar both days

question: Flow through a tube settler basin rises by half during a demand peak. Which consequence should the operator watch for first?
correctAnswer: Carryover of floc as the surface loading rate increases
explanation: Higher flow raises the surface loading rate on the settler, leaving less settling capacity and letting floc carry over to the filters.
options: Freezing of the tube modules at the basin corners
A sudden drop in the raw water chlorine demand
Carryover of floc as the surface loading rate increases
Reversal of the sludge hopper discharge direction

question: After backwashing, a dual media filter shows anthracite mixed deep into the sand layer. Which backwash condition most likely caused the mixing?
correctAnswer: A backwash rate high enough to fully fluidise both layers
explanation: Excessive backwash expansion can intermix the layers; correct expansion lets the denser sand settle below the lighter anthracite.
options: A backwash that ended one minute earlier than usual
A filter run that lasted longer than the day before
A settled water turbidity lower than the plant target
A backwash rate high enough to fully fluidise both layers
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook

optionD: A backwash rate high enough to fully fluidise both layers

question: A plant replaces a serpentine baffle wall arrangement with an open basin layout at the same volume and flow. What happens to the baffling factor the operator can claim?
correctAnswer: It decreases, because short circuiting becomes more likely
explanation: Baffling factors reward plug flow behaviour; an open basin short circuits more, so its baffling factor is lower.
options: It decreases, because short circuiting becomes more likely
It increases, because open water mixes more completely
It stays fixed, because volume alone sets the factor
It becomes equal to the full theoretical detention time
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria

optionD: It becomes equal to the full theoretical detention time

question: Finished water leaving a plant has a strong chlorine taste complaint pattern each morning, with free residual normal by midday. Which breakpoint related cause fits best?
correctAnswer: Dichloramine forming in low flow water overnight in the system
explanation: Dichloramine, which forms on the rising side of the breakpoint curve, has a strong taste and odour and can build up in slow moving water.
options: The clearwell baffles shifting position during the night
Dichloramine forming in low flow water overnight in the system
Raw water ammonia dropping to zero every morning
The chlorine analyser drifting only on sunny mornings
sourceTitle: US EPA: Surface Water Treatment Rules — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Breakpoint Chlorination. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: The clearwell baffles shifting position during the night
optionB: Dichloramine forming in low flow water overnight in the system
optionC: Raw water ammonia dropping to zero every morning
optionD: The chlorine analyser drifting only on sunny mornings

question: An alkalinity titration result comes back far higher than the plant trend. Which error would push the result in that direction?
correctAnswer: Reading the burette at the top of the meniscus each time
explanation: Reading the meniscus inconsistently changes the recorded titrant volume; a consistent eye level reading at the meniscus bottom is required.
options: Using a sample volume smaller than the method states
Letting the indicator fade before recording the volume
Reading the burette at the top of the meniscus each time
Rinsing the flask with the sample before the titration
sourceTitle: WPI: operator examination references — laboratory and treatment study resources

optionB: Letting the indicator fade before recording the volume
optionC: Reading the burette at the top of the meniscus each time
optionD: Rinsing the flask with the sample before the titration

question: Two chemicals delivered the same day are found stored together: ammonium based solution and sodium hypochlorite. What should the operator do first?
correctAnswer: Separate them, because mixing can release chloramine gases
explanation: Hypochlorite mixed with ammonia compounds can release chloramine gases, so incompatible chemicals are separated in storage.
options: Combine them in one tank to save storage floor space
Move both into the chlorine gas room for supervision
Label the pair as compatible and leave them in place
Separate them, because mixing can release chloramine gases

question: A plant treats low alkalinity mountain water and wants to keep coagulation pH in range while raising the alum dose. Which chemical input supports that goal?
correctAnswer: Adding an alkali such as lime or caustic to replace alkalinity
explanation: Supplemental alkalinity from lime or caustic replaces what alum hydrolysis consumes and holds the coagulation pH in range.
options: Adding an alkali such as lime or caustic to replace alkalinity
Adding extra alum ahead of the rapid mix chamber
Adding finished water back into the raw water line
Adding a stronger acid to push the pH downward

question: A jar test shows good settling at 35 mg/L but a cloudy supernatant that will not clear at any dose. Which next step gives the operator useful information?
correctAnswer: Trying a coagulant aid or a different coagulant in the jars
explanation: Persistent cloudiness at every dose suggests the chemistry itself is limiting, so an aid or a different coagulant is tested in the jars.
options: Repeating the same doses with taller beakers only
Trying a coagulant aid or a different coagulant in the jars
Raising the plant dose to double the best jar dose
Settling the jars overnight and using that result

question: A tube settler basin meets its turbidity target at average flow but fails during the two hour morning peak, then recovers. Which design related decision best fits this pattern?
correctAnswer: Equalising or limiting peak flow so loading stays within capacity
explanation: A basin that only fails at peak flow is hydraulically overloaded at the peak, so controlling the peak loading addresses the pattern.
options: Replacing all tube modules with a different colour of plastic
Adding a second sludge blanket level sensor to the basin
Equalising or limiting peak flow so loading stays within capacity
Extending the flocculation time by closing one filter cell
sourceTitle: US EPA: Surface Water Treatment Rules — supporting treatment resources

optionB: Adding a second sludge blanket level sensor to the basin

question: A filter shows turbidity breakthrough at the same point in every run while head loss is still well below its limit. Which investigation step comes first?
correctAnswer: Checking for media loss or a cracked underdrain letting water short circuit
explanation: Repeatable breakthrough at low head loss points to a physical short circuit such as media loss or underdrain damage, not a full bed.
options: Extending the run length to see whether the pattern corrects itself
Raising the backwash rate for the next three washes in a row
Lowering the filter rate and declaring the bed fully restored
Checking for media loss or a cracked underdrain letting water short circuit

optionD: Checking for media loss or a cracked underdrain letting water short circuit

question: Cold water at 5 degrees Celsius slows disinfection in a clearwell that met its CT target all summer at the same residual and T10. Which operator decision responds correctly?
correctAnswer: Raising the residual or contact time to restore the CT credit needed
explanation: Disinfection effectiveness falls as water gets colder, so the operator restores the required CT by raising residual or contact time.
options: Raising the residual or contact time to restore the CT credit needed
Keeping summer settings because CT ignores water temperature
Lowering the residual because cold water holds chlorine longer
Crediting the full basin volume instead of the T10 time

question: A plant doses chlorine past breakpoint on Monday, but by Wednesday the distribution samples show combined residual and no free residual. Which explanation fits best?
correctAnswer: New ammonia entering after treatment is reforming chloramines
explanation: If ammonia enters or is released after breakpoint is passed, free chlorine reacts with it and combined residual reappears.
options: The chlorine cylinders emptied and refilled themselves
New ammonia entering after treatment is reforming chloramines
Breakpoint reactions reversed inside the storage tank
Free chlorine converted into hardness in the mains

question: Duplicate alkalinity titrations differ by a wide margin, and one sample sat uncapped on the bench for an hour before testing. Which quality step addresses the likely error?
correctAnswer: Retesting a fresh sample collected and capped at the sampling point
explanation: An uncapped sample can exchange gases with the air and change before analysis, so a fresh, properly collected sample is retested.
options: Averaging the two results and reporting the mean value
Discarding the lower result because it looks unusual
Retesting a fresh sample collected and capped at the sampling point
Adding extra indicator to the old sample and retitrating

question: A hypochlorite day tank has lost strength faster than expected during a hot week, and dosing pumps are running longer. Which storage decision reduces this decay?
correctAnswer: Keeping the solution shaded, cool and in smaller, fresher batches
explanation: Heat and sunlight speed hypochlorite decay, so cool shaded storage and fresher, smaller batches hold the solution strength longer.
options: Storing the solution in a clear tank on the sunlit side
Topping up old solution with new deliveries each week
Diluting the stored solution with warm water each morning
Keeping the solution shaded, cool and in smaller, fresher batches

question: A plant switches from alum to a ferric coagulant for cold water performance. Which operating consequence should the operator plan for?
correctAnswer: A different alkalinity demand and pH effect to manage in coagulation
explanation: Ferric and alum consume alkalinity at different rates and work over different pH ranges, so the switch changes the alkalinity balance to manage.
options: A different alkalinity demand and pH effect to manage in coagulation
No change at all, because all coagulants behave identically
A complete stop to sludge production from the settling basin
An automatic rise in finished water alkalinity after dosing

question: Jar tests pick 45 mg/L for a high colour water, but the full scale plant performs best at 38 mg/L. Which conclusion is sound for the operator to draw?
correctAnswer: Jar results guide the starting dose and plant performance sets the final dose
explanation: Jar tests approximate plant conditions; the operator starts near the jar result and trims the dose using full scale settled and filtered quality.
options: The jar test must be discarded because it never matches plant results
Jar results guide the starting dose and plant performance sets the final dose
The plant dose should be forced to 45 mg/L to match the jars exactly
Full scale results are unreliable whenever they differ from jar tests

question: A plant blends two raw water sources before coagulation. Source A supplies 800 m3/day at an alkalinity of 140 mg/L as CaCO3, and Source B supplies 200 m3/day at an alkalinity of 90 mg/L as CaCO3. After blending, an alum dose of 36 mg/L is applied, and alum consumes 0.5 mg of alkalinity as CaCO3 per mg of alum. What alkalinity remains after coagulation? Round to 1 decimal place.
explanation: Remaining = ((flow A x alk A + flow B x alk B) / (flow A + flow B)) - (alum dose x factor). Substitution: ((800 x 140 + 200 x 90) / (800 + 200)) - (36 x 0.5) = (130000 / 1000) - 18 = 130 - 18 = 112.0 mg/L. Use the supplied units and assumptions, and round only the final result.
